axes.model_access: The main line is iFlytek's self-developed Spark series — there is an official version-iteration line (V-series version numbers are findable on the official news page); the iFlytek Open Platform (xfyun.cn) is the developer API line, another interface from the same vendor. In-app model tiers are per the signed-in UI.
axes.runtime: Web (xinghuo.xfyun.cn) + iOS/Android apps + PC client; generation is processed on iFlytek's cloud, no model runs locally. The Spark main line does not open-source its weights (unlike DeepSeek/GLM/Qwen).
axes.local_files: Chat history is stored on the account side; document/image parsing happens in the cloud. No locally-oriented data surface declared by the official side.
axes.background: Chats return instantly; no official statement verified for an async task-queue form. The product includes a "deep research"-type long-task capability line (official news-page narrative); whether execution can continue after leaving the page is unverified.
axes.tools: In-product capability lines incl. web search, document parsing, AI writing, problem-solving Q&A and deep research (seen in the official-site navigation); speech capabilities (recognition/synthesis/simultaneous interpretation) are iFlytek's traditional strength and a differentiator inside the product. MCP support not verified item by item.
axes.context: Session history syncs when signed in; no official statement verified for a cross-session memory mechanism (if unknown, say unknown).
axes.permissions: Account system (phone-number registration); the training-use switch path not verified item by item. The Spark model filing number is in the cn block (cross-verified against official public disclosures).
axes.fit: Suits: speech-heavy scenarios (iFlytek's speech foundation is strong), Chinese Q&A + problem-solving, education/office document scenarios. Does not suit: running models locally (Spark does not open-source its weights), or leaving the iFlytek account.
